Use unknown when the evidence cannot establish the requested fact. Do not count supporting facts as completed edits. Assess only the supplied check, not the overall instruction label.

n1: The node’s criterion is broadly appropriate, but its repeated “yes” judgments conflict with the supplied aggregate reference of “partial.” Reassess the edited image against the source and the completion threshold rather than treating any chalk-like appearance as automatically complete: the image retains the giraffes and scene and shows substantial painterly, softened texture, but the evidence should establish whether the result reads as a chalk drawing throughout or only as partial stylization. Distinguish visible progress from full fulfillment using concrete image evidence, and calibrate the label accordingly; do not infer missing edits from the reference label alone. The five high-confidence, near-identical traces indicate a systematic criterion/binding issue, not transport or dependency failure (all executions are valid and complete).
